title: SAP Fiori: SAPUI5 vs OpenUI5 — qué usar
excerpt: Diferencias entre SAPUI5 (comercial) y OpenUI5 (open source).
body:
## OpenUI5
Apache 2.0 open source.
- Free
- Same core UI framework que SAPUI5
- Community-driven contributions
- GitHub: SAP/openui5

## SAPUI5
SAP commercial version:
- Includes OpenUI5 core
- **Plus** premium libraries:
  - sap.suite.ui.commons (business controls)
  - sap.fe.templates (Fiori Elements)
  - sap.ui.comp (smart controls, deprecating)
  - sap.viz.ui5 (charts)
  - sap.ushell (Fiori launchpad)

## Cuándo usar cada uno

### OpenUI5
- Non-SAP web apps que quieren consistent UX
- Learning + experimentation
- Open-source projects

### SAPUI5
- Any SAP-integrated app
- Enterprise apps con Fiori launchpad
- S/4HANA / BTP context

## Availability
### CDN
- OpenUI5: `https://openui5.hana.ondemand.com/`
- SAPUI5: `https://sapui5.hana.ondemand.com/`

### Bundled
S/4HANA + BTP include SAPUI5 automatically.

## Licensing
SAPUI5 requires SAP license (part of SAP subscription).

OpenUI5 no license — free forever.

## Migration OpenUI5 → SAPUI5
Simple: change CDN URL. Core APIs identical.

Add SAPUI5-specific libs si necesitás:
```json
'sap.ui5': {
    'dependencies': {
        'libs': {
            'sap.fe.templates': {}
        }
    }
}
```

## OpenUI5 without SAP
In purely non-SAP projects (public web apps):
- Serve OpenUI5 via CDN
- OData v2/v4 backend (any framework)
- Deploy anywhere (Netlify, Vercel, AWS)

## Popular OpenUI5 uses
- Portals
- Employee-facing apps
- Custom dashboards
- Prototypes

## Common questions

### 'Fiori Elements' available in OpenUI5?
No. Requires `sap.fe.templates` (SAPUI5 only).

### Basic apps work with OpenUI5?
Yes. sap.m + sap.ui.core suffice for most freestyle apps.

### Fiori launchpad works with OpenUI5?
No. Launchpad is SAPUI5 (`sap.ushell`).

OpenUI5 apps can be standalone o hosted in own launcher.

## Version parity
OpenUI5 y SAPUI5 same version numbers y release cadence.

OpenUI5 tarda ~1-2 weeks después de SAPUI5 release (community catchup).

## Best practices
- **New SAP dev**: use SAPUI5
- **Independent web app**: OpenUI5 is fine
- **Test with OpenUI5** if want portability

title: SAP Fiori: SAPUI5 CDN vs bundled resources
excerpt: Choose between CDN o bundled UI5.
body:
## Bundled
SAPUI5 files hosted en your own server.

### Ventajas
- No internet dependency
- Faster (local network)
- Enterprise firewalls comfortable

### Desventajas
- Storage cost
- Manual updates
- Serve 100s MB of UI5 files

## CDN
SAP-hosted:
- `https://sapui5.hana.ondemand.com/1.120.5/resources/sap-ui-core.js`

### Ventajas
- Latest version easily
- Cached by browsers (may already have from other sites)
- No local storage
- SAP maintains

### Desventajas
- Internet required
- Corporate firewalls may block
- Latency depends on location

## Config
### CDN
index.html:
```html
<script id='sap-ui-bootstrap'
    src='https://sapui5.hana.ondemand.com/1.120.5/resources/sap-ui-core.js'
    data-sap-ui-theme='sap_horizon'
    data-sap-ui-libs='sap.m,sap.ui.core'
    data-sap-ui-resourceroots='{'com.empresa.miapp': './'}'></script>
```

### Bundled
```html
<script id='sap-ui-bootstrap'
    src='/resources/sap-ui-core.js'
    data-sap-ui-theme='sap_horizon'></script>
```

UI5 files under `/resources/`.

## Version locking
Bundled: version fixed until manually updated.
CDN: option to specify exact version en URL.

### Latest
```html
<script src='https://sapui5.hana.ondemand.com/resources/sap-ui-core.js'></script>
```

**Not recommended en production** — surprise breakage on SAP updates.

### Pin version
```html
<script src='https://sapui5.hana.ondemand.com/1.120.5/resources/sap-ui-core.js'></script>
```

Recommended.

## Fiori launchpad automatic
Launchpad server bundles UI5. Apps hosted there don't need to think about this.

## Preload
Bundling multiple files into `Component-preload.js`:
```bash
npx @ui5/cli build
```

Reduces # HTTP requests.

## Corporate CDN
Some enterprises mirror UI5 en their internal CDN:
- Cloudflare / Akamai
- Corporate edge servers

Combina CDN benefits + local network speed.

## Offline
Bundle required. CDN no funciona offline.

## Best practices
- **Production**: pin version, use CDN or corporate mirror
- **Development**: latest CDN OK
- **Air-gapped environments**: fully bundled
- **Migration to newer version**: update CDN URL, test, then deploy

title: SAP Fiori: SAPUI5 debug mode
excerpt: Enable debug mode for troubleshooting Fiori apps.
body:
## Enable debug mode

### Method 1: URL parameter
Append `?sap-ui-debug=true`

Loads unminified UI5 source, better stack traces.

### Method 2: Support Assistant
`Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P` en app → tab **Support**.

### Method 3: Debug all
`sap-ui-debug=all` — loads even more diagnostic info.

## Log level
```
?sap-ui-log-level=DEBUG
```

Levels:
- FATAL
- ERROR
- WARNING
- INFO
- DEBUG
- TRACE

DEBUG floods console con detailed info.

## Support Assistant
Built-in analyzer:
1. Open app
2. Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P
3. Tab **Support**
4. **Run rule set**
5. Get report:
   - Deprecation warnings
   - Best practice violations
   - Performance issues

## UI5 diagnostics window
Ctrl+Alt+Shift+S — floating window:
- Elements tree
- Bindings
- Models
- Routing

## Data binding inspector
Ctrl+Alt+Shift+P → **Technical Info → Bindings** → tree of active bindings.

Useful para debug why field not updating.

## Element inspector
Click UI element in inspector → highlight in DOM.

### Direct: Chrome DevTools
Regular DevTools → Elements → find UI5 element by class `sapMBtn`, `sapMInput`, etc.

## OData request tracer
```javascript
var oModel = new sap.ui.model.odata.v2.ODataModel(url);
oModel.attachRequestSent(e => console.log('SENT:', e.getParameters()));
oModel.attachRequestCompleted(e => console.log('OK:', e.getParameters()));
oModel.attachRequestFailed(e => console.error('FAIL:', e.getParameters()));
```

O enable via config:
```html
data-sap-ui-xx-debugmodulesForRealTimeError='xxx'
```

## Log to server
For prod issues user can't reproduce:
```javascript
var oLog = jQuery.sap.log;
oLog.setLevel(jQuery.sap.log.Level.DEBUG);

oLog.addLogListener({
    onLogEntry: function(logEntry) {
        fetch('/api/log', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(logEntry) });
    }
});
```

## Common issues + debug approach

### 'Nothing happens on button click'
- Console errors? Uncaught exceptions?
- Event handler correctly bound?

### 'Data not showing'
- Network tab: OData responded?
- Model set on view?
- Binding path correct? Debug con `oModel.getData()`

### 'App slow'
- Enable performance profiler (DevTools)
- Check N+1 queries en Network tab
- Look for tight loops

### 'Fires multiple times'
- Event listener attached twice
- onInit called on view instance recreation
- Add debounce/throttle

## Version info
```
sap.ui.version   // '1.120.5'
sap.ui.getCore().getConfiguration()   // config object
```

## Best practices
- **Never enable full debug en prod** (performance impact)
- **Support Assistant rules** run monthly
- **Test error scenarios** — not just happy paths
- **User feedback → correlate con logs**

title: SAP Fiori: security headers y CSP
excerpt: Content Security Policy y otros security headers.
body:
## HTTP security headers
Proteger apps Fiori/SAPUI5 from common attacks.

## Content Security Policy (CSP)
Whitelisting allowed sources of scripts, styles, images:

```
Content-Security-Policy: 
    default-src 'self';
    script-src 'self' https://sapui5.hana.ondemand.com;
    style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline';
    img-src 'self' data: https:;
    connect-src 'self' https://api.mybackend.com;
    frame-ancestors 'none';
```

### Directives
- **default-src** — fallback for others
- **script-src** — where JS can load from
- **style-src** — CSS sources
- **img-src** — images
- **connect-src** — XHR / fetch destinations
- **frame-ancestors** — who can iframe this app (`'none'` = nobody)
- **font-src** — fonts
- **media-src** — audio/video

## Fiori-friendly CSP
SAPUI5 needs some flexibility. Common baseline:
```
script-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval' https://*.hana.ondemand.com;
style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://*.hana.ondemand.com;
img-src 'self' data: blob: https:;
connect-src 'self' https://*.hana.ondemand.com;
font-src 'self' data: https://*.hana.ondemand.com;
```

### 'unsafe-eval' needed for
SAPUI5 uses eval internally. Cannot fully block.

### 'unsafe-inline' style-src
Some inline styles unavoidable en SAPUI5.

## Configure en app router
`xs-app.json`:
```json
{
    'authenticationMethod': 'route',
    'welcomeFile': '/index.html',
    'sessionTimeout': 30,
    'websockets': { 'enabled': true },
    'routes': [...],
    'responseHeaders': [
        {
            'name': 'Content-Security-Policy',
            'value': "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval' https://*.hana.ondemand.com; ..."
        },
        {
            'name': 'X-Content-Type-Options',
            'value': 'nosniff'
        },
        {
            'name': 'X-Frame-Options',
            'value': 'SAMEORIGIN'
        },
        {
            'name': 'Strict-Transport-Security',
            'value': 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains'
        }
    ]
}
```

## Other important headers

### X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
Prevents MIME sniffing attacks.

### X-Frame-Options: DENY / SAMEORIGIN
Prevents clickjacking.

### Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)
Force HTTPS:
```
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload
```

### Referrer-Policy
```
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
```

### Permissions-Policy (newer)
Control browser features:
```
Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(self)
```

## XSS protection
SAPUI5 built-in:
- Text bindings HTML-encoded automáticamente
- URL sanitization
- HTML sanitization en RichText controls

Don't disable sanitization unless absolutely necessary.

### Careful
```xml
<!-- Dangerous -->
<FormattedText htmlText='{Description}'/>
<!-- If Description contains <script>, could be executed -->
```

Use sanitization:
```javascript
var sHtml = jQuery.sap.encodeHTML(input);
// Then set as htmlText
```

## CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery)
### SAP standard
OData services require `X-CSRF-Token`:
1. GET request → server returns token
2. Include token en subsequent POST/PUT/DELETE

SAPUI5 model handles automatically.

## Cookies
### HttpOnly
Prevent JS access to session cookies:
```
Set-Cookie: session=xxx; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict
```

### Secure
Only send over HTTPS.

### SameSite
Protection contra CSRF.

## Test
### Automated
- Mozilla Observatory: https://observatory.mozilla.org/
- Security Headers: https://securityheaders.com/

### Manual
Check response headers en DevTools Network tab.

## Common issues

### CSP blocks CDN scripts
Adjust `script-src` to include CDN URLs.

### 'unsafe-eval' warnings
SAPUI5 requires it. Reduce risk elsewhere (input sanitization).

### Fiori launchpad iframe issues
`X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` may block. Launchpad hosts apps in iframes.

## Best practices
- **All headers** — no just CSP
- **HTTPS-only** — never HTTP en prod
- **Regular audits** — new attack vectors emerge
- **Balance security vs functionality** — over-strict CSP breaks apps

title: SAP Fiori: SAPUI5 in embedded scenarios (iframe)
excerpt: Embed Fiori apps en portals externos u otros apps.
body:
## Escenarios
- Embed Fiori en corporate portal
- Embed en Confluence, SharePoint
- Cross-app embedding

## iframe basics
```html
<iframe src='https://myapp.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com/' width='100%' height='600'></iframe>
```

### Requirements para funcionar
- Fiori app allows framing (X-Frame-Options)
- Auth (SSO or embedded login)
- Communication host↔iframe (postMessage)

## X-Frame-Options
### DENY
No iframing possible.

### SAMEORIGIN
Only iframe desde same origin.

### Removed / not set
Any origin can iframe (least secure).

Fiori launchpad apps: SAMEORIGIN default.

## CSP frame-ancestors
Modern replacement:
```
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' https://portal.empresa.com
```

Whitelist specific domains.

## Auth propagation
### SSO via SAML
If both host + iframe use same IdP:
- User authenticated en host
- iframe auto-authenticates via SSO redirect
- Session cookies passed

### Cookies + SameSite
SameSite=Strict blocks iframe cookies.
SameSite=Lax OK for GET.
SameSite=None + Secure required for iframe.

## postMessage communication
Host ↔ iframe:

### Iframe → host
```javascript
window.parent.postMessage({ event: 'action', data: { ... } }, 'https://portal.empresa.com');
```

### Host receives
```javascript
window.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
    if (event.origin !== 'https://myapp.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com') return;
    console.log('Iframe says:', event.data);
});
```

### Host → iframe
```javascript
var iframe = document.getElementById('myFiori');
iframe.contentWindow.postMessage({ event: 'reload' }, 'https://myapp.cfapps.eu10.hana.ondemand.com');
```

Security: always verify `event.origin`.

## Fiori launchpad handles this
`sap.ushell.services.CrossApplicationNavigation`:
- Ejemplo intent → app opened en iframe
- App emits events → launchpad receives
- Consistent framework

## Sizing
```javascript
// Iframe reports height to parent
window.parent.postMessage({
    event: 'resize',
    height: document.body.scrollHeight
}, '*');
```

Parent adjusts iframe height dynamically.

## Session sharing
### Same origin
Cookies shared → session shared automáticamente.

### Cross-origin
More complex — each site has own session.
Coordinate via SAML/OIDC federation.

## Common issues

### 'Cannot iframe: X-Frame-Options'
App server explicitly denies iframing. Config change needed.

### 'Blocked by CSP'
Host página tiene CSP muy restrictive. Whitelist iframe domain.

### 'Session lost'
Cookies SameSite issue. Config SameSite=None + Secure.

### 'Broken layout'
iframe sizing wrong. Use postMessage sizing.

## SAP Companion (moderno)
SAP tiene SAP Companion — allows embedding apps con SAP standards.

## Best practices
- **Minimize embedding** — often better standalone or launchpad
- **Validate origin** en postMessage
- **HTTPS everywhere**
- **Test cross-browser** — some behaviors differ

title: SAP Fiori: comunes 'gotchas' y patterns
excerpt: Trampas comunes y patterns established para evitarlas.

title: SAP Fiori: migrate from SAPUI5 freestyle → Fiori Elements
excerpt: Cuándo y cómo migrar apps custom a Fiori Elements.
body:
## Cuándo migrar

### Buenos candidatos
- Standard CRUD apps (create/read/update/delete)
- List + detail patterns
- Reporting con OData source
- Apps con lot of custom code que replica Fiori Elements features

### Malos candidatos
- Highly custom UX
- Complex workflows
- Non-standard interactions
- Where Fiori Elements limitations block business needs

## Migration steps

### 1. Assess current freestyle app
Document:
- Entities used
- Views (list, detail, forms)
- Custom actions
- Business logic
- Integrations

### 2. Map to Fiori Elements template
- List + detail → **List Report Object Page**
- Dashboard → **Overview Page**
- Analytics → **Analytical List Page**
- Task list → **Worklist**

### 3. Ensure OData service compatible
- OData v4 preferred
- Annotations required (or add en CDS)
- Draft-enabled si edit needed

### 4. Regenerate app con Fiori Elements template
```bash
npx @sap/generator-fiori
```

Choose template. Point to existing OData service.

### 5. Add annotations
For each entity, define:
- UI.LineItem (columns)
- UI.HeaderInfo
- UI.FieldGroup
- UI.SelectionFields
- Actions

### 6. Migrate custom logic
- Formatters → same pattern
- Actions → OData actions
- Custom validation → CAP handlers
- Custom UI sections → extension points

### 7. Test
- Same functional coverage
- Compare user experience side-by-side
- Get user feedback

### 8. Deploy alongside original
Blue/green:
- Old app: `/oldapp`
- New app: `/newapp`
- Redirect users gradually

### 9. Sunset original
Después user validation, retire old app.

## Extension points
Fiori Elements allows custom extensions:
- Custom actions
- Custom sections en Object Page
- Custom columns con computed values
- Overrides de behavior

### Custom section
```json
// manifest.json
'extends': {
    'extensions': {
        'sap.ui.controllerExtensions': {
            'sap.fe.templates.ObjectPage.ObjectPageController': {
                'controllerName': 'com.empresa.ext.controller.ObjectPageExt'
            }
        }
    }
}
```

## Common challenges

### 'Feature X not supported en Fiori Elements'
- Assess feature necessity
- Either accept limitation or extension
- Sometimes freestyle warranted

### 'Backend doesn't have annotations'
- Add CAP CDS annotations if backend is CAP
- Add annotations via `.cds` file for external OData
- SAP annotation modeler

### 'Learning curve for team'
- Training on Fiori Elements + CAP
- Pair with experienced Fiori Elements dev

### 'Existing bookmarks / navigation'
Old app URL structure differs. Provide redirects.

## Benefits post-migration
- Less code to maintain (60-80% reduction común)
- SAP-standard UX (users familiar)
- Automatic Fiori guideline compliance
- Future updates from SAP inherit for free

## Costs
- Migration effort (weeks-months)
- Some UX changes (users may complain initially)
- Testing effort

## Not-migrating alternatives
Some apps stay freestyle indefinitely:
- Highly custom
- Legacy support required
- Small enough that Fiori Elements overhead not worth

Evaluate case-by-case.

## Best practices
- **Pilot with 1 app** first
- **Involve users** — get feedback early
- **Document** annotations pattern
- **Extensions minimally** — try Fiori Elements first

title: SAP Cloud Connector: log analysis con SIEM
excerpt: Ingesting SCC logs en SIEM enterprise.
body:
## Logs disponibles

### Access log
Every request via tunnel. Fields:
- Timestamp
- User
- Backend virtual host + URL
- HTTP method
- Status code
- Response time
- Bytes

### Audit log
Admin actions:
- Login/logout
- Config changes
- Cert operations

### Trace log
Debugging only. High volume, low value in prod.

### System log
SCC service health.

## Log locations
### Linux
`/opt/sap/scc/log/`:
- `access.log`
- `audit.log`
- `scc_daemon.log`
- `subaccount_*.log`

### Windows
`%ProgramData%\SAP\SAP Cloud Connector\log\`

## Splunk integration

### Universal Forwarder
Install on SCC server. Config `inputs.conf`:
```
[monitor:///opt/sap/scc/log/audit.log]
index = scc
sourcetype = scc:audit

[monitor:///opt/sap/scc/log/access.log]
index = scc
sourcetype = scc:access
```

Forwards logs to Splunk indexers.

### Splunk queries
```
index=scc sourcetype=scc:audit level=WARNING
| stats count by user, action

index=scc sourcetype=scc:access status>=500
| timechart count by virtualhost
```

## Elasticsearch (ELK)

### Filebeat
```yaml
# filebeat.yml
filebeat.inputs:
- type: log
  paths:
    - /opt/sap/scc/log/*.log
  fields:
    service: scc

output.elasticsearch:
  hosts: ['elasticsearch:9200']
```

### Kibana dashboards
- Access rate
- Error rate
- Top errors
- Latency

## Sentinel (Azure)

### Log Analytics Agent
1. Install en SCC server
2. Config log path collection
3. Data streams to Log Analytics workspace
4. Sentinel queries KQL

```kql
SCC_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where SeverityLevel_s == 'ERROR'
| summarize count() by Message_s
```

## Native SCC syslog
SCC UI → **Configuration → Log And Trace → Audit Log → Syslog**:
- Server host + port
- Format: RFC3164, RFC5424

UDP or TCP.

## Correlation

### Request ID header
BTP app sends `X-Correlation-Id: abc123`.
SCC logs it.
Backend receives it.

Correlate en SIEM across all layers.

### Timestamp precision
SCC millisecond precision. Sync clocks via NTP.

## Alerts en SIEM

### Splunk alerts
```
index=scc source=/opt/sap/scc/log/audit.log 'Config change'
| stats count by user
| where count > 5
```

Alert: user changed config 5+ times in an hour → suspicious.

### Failed auth
```
index=scc 'Authentication failed'
| stats count by client_ip
| where count > 10
```

## Retention
### Local SCC
7 días access log default, 90 días audit.

### SIEM
Longer retention: 1-3 years typical for compliance.

## Compliance queries
- Who accessed customer data (audit + access log join)?
- Who changed config (audit log)?
- Failed access attempts (access log 401/403)?
- Certificate expiry approaching?

## Ingestion cost
SCC generates ~1-10 GB/day per active tunnel.

SIEM licensed by data volume — factor into TCO.

### Reduce
- Filter access log to errors only
- Sample high-volume services
- Aggregate on ingestion

## Best practices
- **Structured logging** (JSON) — easier parsing
- **Central SIEM** — not scattered logs
- **Automated alerts** — anomalies caught quickly
- **Regular review** — dashboards actionable
- **Retention policy** — matches compliance

title: SAP Cloud Connector: HTTPS destinations config avanzado
excerpt: Configuraciones avanzadas de HTTPS con SCC.
body:
## Escenarios avanzados

### 1. mTLS a backend
Backend requiere client cert. SCC provides.

Cubrimos en artículo mTLS.

### 2. HTTP/2
SCC forwards HTTP/2 request/response:
- Backend soporta HTTP/2? Config enable
- Multiplexing benefits

### 3. HTTPS con self-signed cert backend
SCC config: **Trust Store → Import CA** del backend.

### 4. Certificate pinning
App BTP con cert pinning:
- Cert of backend hardcoded en app
- SCC forwards raw — pin verifies backend cert directly

### 5. TLS 1.3 support
SCC 2.15+ soporta TLS 1.3.
Backend + client también deben soportarlo.

### 6. Custom cipher suites
SCC config → **Cryptography → Cipher Suites**:
- Enable strong ciphers only
- Disable weak (RC4, DES, 3DES)

### 7. SNI (Server Name Indication)
Backend hosts multiple certs on same IP. SCC sends SNI en TLS handshake.

Automatic si backend needs it.

### 8. Cert chain validation
SCC validates full chain. Chain incomplete? Import intermediates en trust store.

### 9. OCSP / CRL
SCC checks revocation. If OCSP server slow, may cause timeouts.

Disable si necesario (compliance permitting):
- Java system property `-Dcom.sun.net.ssl.checkRevocation=false`

### 10. Cert expiry monitoring
SCC UI dashboard shows cert expiry.

Alert email configurable.

## Debugging TLS issues

### Enable TLS trace
SCC UI → **Log And Trace → Trace Level = DEBUG**.

SCC log contendrá TLS handshake details.

### openssl testing
From SCC server:
```bash
openssl s_client -connect backend.local:443 -servername backend.local
```

Verify:
- Cert chain OK
- TLS version negotiated
- Cipher

### Wireshark
Capture on SCC server:
- Filter `ssl or tls`
- View handshake, cert exchange
- Diagnose failures

## Common errors

### 'PKIX path building failed'
Missing CA in trust store.

### 'Cert expired'
Update backend cert.

### 'CN mismatch'
Cert Common Name doesn't match hostname requested.

### 'No cipher suites in common'
SCC + backend don't share supported ciphers. Update one or both.

### 'Protocol version mismatch'
SCC configured for TLS 1.3, backend only TLS 1.2. Lower SCC minimum.

## Best practices
- **TLS 1.2 minimum** everywhere
- **Strong ciphers only**
- **Cert rotation proactive** — 30 days before expiry
- **Chain complete** en backend
- **Monitor OCSP/CRL health**

title: SAP Cloud Connector: version compatibility matrix
excerpt: Compatibilidad SCC con Java, JRE, BTP.
body:
## Java compatibility

### SCC 2.15+ (current)
- Java 17 recommended (SapMachine 17)
- Java 11 supported (deprecating)
- Java 8 no supported

### Older SCC 2.13, 2.14
- Java 11 or 8 supported

### Legacy 2.10-2.12
- Java 8 only

## OS compatibility

### Windows
- Windows Server 2019, 2022
- Windows 10, 11 (dev only)

### Linux
- RHEL 8, 9
- SLES 15
- Ubuntu 20.04, 22.04
- Rocky, Alma (RHEL clones)

## Browser (UI)
- Chrome 100+
- Edge 100+
- Firefox 100+
- Safari 15+

## BTP compatibility
SCC works with all BTP regions.

### Tunnel protocol
- BTP-standard TLS-based tunnel
- SCC negotiates supported protocol version con BTP
- Latest SCC recommended for new features

### Feature parity
Older SCC → some new BTP features unavailable:
- Latest SCC always for enterprise

## Backend compatibility

### SAP systems
- ECC 6.0+
- S/4HANA (all versions)
- BW 7.5+
- HANA (all versions)
- Solman 7.2+

### Non-SAP
- Any HTTP-based (REST, SOAP, OData)
- Any TCP-based (LDAP, JDBC, custom)
- LDAPS (Active Directory)

## SCC-to-SCC compatibility (HA)
Master/Shadow must be SAME version. Cross-version HA not supported.

Upgrade rolling:
1. Upgrade Shadow
2. Test
3. Failover Master → Shadow
4. Upgrade Master
5. Failback (or leave as swapped)

## API compatibility
SCC REST API:
- Version 1 (stable)
- Backwards compatible con older clients
- New endpoints in newer versions

## Config file compatibility
### Export from newer → import to older
No supported. May silently corrupt config.

### Export from older → import to newer
Supported (SCC auto-migrates config format).

## Best practices
- **Latest LTS Java** (SapMachine 17)
- **Latest SCC** every 6-12 months
- **Test upgrade** en staging first
- **Same version** across HA pair
- **Backup config** before upgrade

title: SAP Cloud Connector: BTP Kyma runtime integration
excerpt: Usar SCC desde Kyma runtime apps.
body:
## Kyma runtime
Kubernetes-based runtime en BTP:
- Full K8s power
- Serverless functions
- Event-driven

## Consumo desde Kyma
Similar a CF, apps Kyma consumen SCC via:
1. Connectivity service instance
2. Destination service
3. XSUAA (auth)

## Setup

### 1. Bind services
```yaml
apiVersion: services.cloud.sap.com/v1
kind: ServiceInstance
metadata:
    name: connectivity
spec:
    serviceOfferingName: connectivity
    servicePlanName: lite
---
apiVersion: services.cloud.sap.com/v1
kind: ServiceBinding
metadata:
    name: connectivity-binding
spec:
    serviceInstanceName: connectivity
```

### 2. Deployment con service bindings
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
spec:
    template:
        spec:
            containers:
            - name: my-app
              env:
              - name: BINDINGS_CONNECTIVITY
                valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                        name: connectivity-binding
                        key: credentials
            - name: BINDINGS_DESTINATION
                valueFrom: ...
```

### 3. App code
Read creds del env var:
```javascript
const creds = JSON.parse(process.env.BINDINGS_CONNECTIVITY);
// Use onpremise_proxy_host, port
```

## SAP Cloud SDK
Handles complexity:
```javascript
const { executeHttpRequest } = require('@sap-cloud-sdk/http-client');
const response = await executeHttpRequest({ destinationName: 'MY_ECC' });
```

SDK detects Kyma context, uses correct bindings.

## Serverless functions con SCC
Kyma functions:
```javascript
module.exports = {
    main: async (event, context) => {
        const dest = await getDestination('MY_ECC');
        const response = await fetch(dest.url);
        return { data: response };
    }
};
```

Functions can call on-prem via SCC.

## Networking

### Egress via Istio
Kyma uses Istio service mesh. Egress al SCC endpoint:
- Automatic con destination config
- ServiceEntry para custom routing

### Ingress
APIs exposed via APIRule (Istio-based).

## Difference vs CF

### CF
- Buildpack-based apps
- CLI-driven (cf push)
- Simpler for basic apps

### Kyma
- Container-based (Docker)
- K8s-native (kubectl, Helm)
- More flexible
- Event-driven capabilities native

## Choose
- **CF**: simpler apps, teams sin K8s expertise
- **Kyma**: cloud-native, complex apps, event-driven, use K8s ecosystem

## SCC config unchanged
Same SCC serves both CF + Kyma workloads. No dual setup.

## Migration CF → Kyma
Some orgs migrate:
- Containerize CF apps
- Deploy to Kyma
- Consume services same way

Effort varies. Migration tool available (limited).

## Common issues

### 'Service binding not found'
- Kubernetes secret missing
- Verify ServiceBinding status: `kubectl get servicebinding`

### 'Destination not configured'
- Same as CF: BTP subaccount destination config

### 'Slow response'
- Kyma serverless functions have cold start
- Provision more replicas for hot path

## Best practices
- **SDK usage** — abstracts complexity
- **Health checks** — K8s liveness/readiness
- **Autoscaling** — Kyma supports HPA
- **Same monitoring** as regular K8s

title: SAP Cloud Connector: consumo desde apps ABAP Cloud (Steampunk)
tags: scc, abap cloud, steampunk, http destination
excerpt: ABAP en BTP consuming on-prem via SCC.
body:
## Context
ABAP Environment (Steampunk) is ABAP en BTP. Apps ABAP corriendo en cloud.

Para comunicarse con on-prem SAP:
- SCC tunnel
- BTP destination
- Communication arrangement en ABAP

## Setup

### 1. SCC (already deployed)
- Subaccount registered
- On-prem system exposed as virtual host
- Resource whitelisted

### 2. BTP destination
Subaccount → **Destinations → New**:
- Name: `MY_ECC_ONPREM`
- URL: `https://virtual-ecc:443`
- ProxyType: OnPremise
- Auth: BasicAuth / OAuth / PrincipalPropagation

### 3. Communication scenario (ABAP)
In ABAP Environment:
1. `SAP Fiori launchpad → Communication Arrangements`
2. **New**:
    - Scenario: standard o custom Z_MI_SCENARIO
    - Arrangement name: `CA_ECC_ONPREM`
    - Communication system: link a destination
    - Communication user: mapping

### 4. Consume from ABAP
```abap
DATA(destination) = cl_http_destination_provider=>create_by_comm_arrangement(
    comm_scenario = 'Z_MI_SCENARIO'
    service_id = 'Z_ECC_SERVICE'
).

DATA(http_client) = cl_web_http_client_manager=>create_by_http_destination( destination ).
DATA(request) = http_client->get_http_request( ).
request->set_header_field( name = 'Accept' value = 'application/json' ).

DATA(response) = http_client->execute( if_web_http_client=>get ).
DATA(body) = response->get_text( ).
```

## Common patterns

### Call OData service en ECC
```abap
DATA(url) = |/sap/opu/odata/sap/API_BUSINESS_PARTNER/A_BusinessPartner('{ id }')|.
request->set_url( url ).
response = http_client->execute( if_web_http_client=>get ).
```

### Call RFC (via SM59)
SCC config as RFC destination. ABAP calls RFC:
```abap
CALL FUNCTION 'BAPI_BUSPARTNER_GET' DESTINATION 'MY_RFC_ONPREM'
    EXPORTING businesspartner = '1000'
    IMPORTING ... .
```

## Principal propagation
User identity propagates:
- ABAP Cloud app runs as User A (from JWT)
- Call to on-prem: User A's identity forwarded via SCC
- On-prem ECC honors User A's authorizations

Requires trust config (SAML) between ABAP Cloud + ECC.

## Error handling
```abap
TRY.
    response = http_client->execute( if_web_http_client=>get ).
    IF response->get_status( )-code >= 400.
      " Handle error
    ENDIF.
  CATCH cx_web_http_client_error INTO DATA(exception).
    " Network / SCC error
ENDTRY.
```

## Auth types
- **BasicAuthentication** — user + pass en destination
- **OAuth2** — token flows
- **PrincipalPropagation** — user identity chain
- **ClientCert** — X.509 mTLS

## Common issues

### 'Destination not found'
- Communication arrangement missing
- Or destination not visible en subaccount

### '401 Unauthorized'
- Auth config incorrect
- Or user lacks backend auth

### 'SSL handshake failure'
- Cert issue en trust chain
- Update SCC + ECC trust

### Timeout
- Backend slow
- Increase timeout en destination

## Autorización
ABAP Cloud roles determine who can consume communication arrangements.

On-prem ECC roles determine what functions/data accessible.

Both needed.

## Best practices
- **Communication arrangements** — no hardcoded URLs en ABAP code
- **Error handling** — anticipate SCC/backend failures
- **Retry logic** — transient failures common
- **Monitoring** — log all outbound calls

title: SAP Cloud Connector: SAP Cloud Integration (CPI) via SCC
excerpt: iFlows CPI que consumen backends on-prem.
body:
## Context
CPI (Cloud Integration) es BTP service. iFlows procesan messages between systems.

Con SCC, iFlows pueden llegar a on-prem SAP.

## Config

### 1. SCC + subaccount
SCC connected to subaccount que hosts CPI.

### 2. Backend exposed en SCC
On-prem system con virtual host + resource whitelist.

### 3. Cloud connector destination en CPI
CPI tenant → **Monitoring → Manage Security → Cloud Connector**:
- Verify SCC visible
- Location ID si aplica

### 4. iFlow receiver adapter
Create iFlow. Sender doesn't matter (HTTP, timer, etc.).

Receiver adapter type:
- **HTTP** — REST call to virtual host
- **OData v2/v4** — OData call
- **RFC** — for RFC destinations
- **SOAP** — SOAP endpoints

Adapter config:
- **ProxyType**: **On-Premise** (critical)
- **Location ID**: si multi-SCC
- **Address**: virtual host from SCC
- **Auth**: BasicAuth con user/pass, o PrincipalPropagation

## Ejemplo iFlow
```
[HTTP Sender] → [Content Modifier] → [Message Mapping] → [OData Receiver] (to on-prem S/4)
```

External system POSTs to iFlow → transformed → sent to on-prem S/4 via SCC.

## Auth patterns

### Basic auth con technical user
Simplest. Not user-specific.

### Principal propagation
Original caller's identity flows through:
- App → CPI → SCC → on-prem

Requires SAML trust setup.

### OAuth2 con client credentials
Machine-to-machine. Cert-based rotation.

## Testing
### CPI simulate
1. iFlow → **Simulate**
2. Provide sample payload
3. Trace through steps
4. Ver output

### Real invoke
curl / Postman to iFlow endpoint.

## Monitoring
CPI → **Monitoring → Message Processing**:
- Success / error
- Payload inspection
- Retry

## Common issues

### 'Cannot connect: onpremise'
- ProxyType not set to OnPremise
- SCC not connected
- Backend not exposed

### 'Authentication failed'
- User creds wrong en destination
- Or PP trust config broken

### 'Certificate not trusted'
- Backend cert self-signed, not en SCC trust store
- Import CA

## Error handling en iFlow
### Exception subprocess
Catch errors, log, notify:
```
[Main flow] → catches errors → [Exception subprocess: log + retry + alert]
```

### Dead letter queue
Failed messages → separate queue for manual inspection.

## Async patterns
### JMS queue
Buffer messages en queue. iFlow processes async.

### AS2/EDI
Document exchange con trading partners.

## Message transformation
CPI shines for:
- JSON ↔ XML
- IDoc ↔ REST
- SAP EDI ↔ ANSI X12
- SOAP ↔ REST

Use mapping steps (graphical o Groovy scripts).

## Rate limiting
CPI + SCC combo can produce heavy load. Configure:
- iFlow polling frequency
- SCC rate limits per resource
- Backend capacity monitoring

## Best practices
- **Idempotency** — retries should not duplicate
- **Structured logging** — searchable en CPI monitor
- **Timeouts explicitly set**
- **Test error paths** — not just happy path
- **Version iFlows** en Git (CPI has git integration)

title: SAP Cloud Connector: onboarding new team members
excerpt: Cómo capacitar a nuevos admins de SCC.
body:
## Perfil del rol
SCC admin needs:
- OS admin (Linux + Windows)
- Networking basics (TCP/IP, TLS, proxies)
- Java runtime familiarity
- SAP integration concepts
- Security awareness

## Onboarding steps

### Week 1: fundamentos
- Read SAP help docs
- Complete OpenSAP course 'SAP BTP Cloud Connectivity'
- Understand SCC purpose + arquitecture
- Ver diagrama del landscape

### Week 2: hands-on
- Get access a SCC UI (dev/staging)
- Explore configuration
- Read existing subaccount configs
- Ver access logs, audit logs
- Runbook walkthrough

### Week 3: shadow
- Pair with senior admin
- Watch config changes
- Ver troubleshoot session
- Attend incident response

### Week 4: guided tasks
- Do a config change (with review)
- Handle a minor issue
- Contribute to documentation

## Documentation to prepare

### Architecture doc
- Diagram of SCC placement en landscape
- List of subaccounts + purposes
- List of exposed systems + resources
- Users + roles
- SLA + RTO/RPO targets

### Runbook
- Common tasks step-by-step
- Add new subaccount
- Add new system + resource
- Renew cert
- Handle tunnel disconnect
- Restart SCC service
- Backup/restore

### Runbook para incidentes
- Tunnel down
- Backend unreachable
- Cert expired
- Config corruption

Escalation:
- Who to call
- SAP support process

### Config baseline
Document approved config:
- Which subaccounts
- Which systems
- Auth methods
- HA setup

Audit against baseline.

## Access management

### For newcomers
- Read-only first (`Display` role)
- Watch, learn
- No production changes

### After 1-2 months
- Support role (limited changes)
- Reboot, cert import
- No admin

### After proven competence
- Admin role
- Config changes con approval

## Regular training
- Quarterly: review latest features (SCC releases)
- Semi-annual: security best practices
- Annual: DR drill

## Communication
- Slack channel: `#scc-team`
- Weekly team meeting
- Shared calendar: cert expiry dates

## Escalation
- L1: helpdesk (basic)
- L2: SCC admin team
- L3: senior architect
- L4: SAP support

## Retention
SCC expertise valuable. Cross-train multiple people:
- No single point of knowledge failure
- Bus factor > 1

## Tools
- Access: SSH to SCC server, RDP to Windows
- Monitoring: Splunk / Grafana access
- Documentation: Confluence, SharePoint
- Ticketing: JIRA, ServiceNow

## Metrics
Onboarding success:
- Time to first competent solo change
- # of incidents handled correctly
- Feedback from team

Target: 3 months to fully productive.

## Best practices
- **Documentation** — living document
- **Pair regularly** — knowledge sharing
- **Rotate on-call** — no burnout
- **Learn from incidents** — postmortems
- **Recognize expertise** — internal certifications

title: SAP Cloud Connector: SLA + operational metrics
excerpt: Definir + medir SLAs de SCC.
body:
## Service Level Objectives (SLOs)
Internal targets:
- Availability: 99.9% (43 min downtime/month)
- Latency: p99 < 500 ms
- Error rate: <1%

## SLIs (Service Level Indicators)
Métricas para medir:

### Availability
- Tunnel state (Connected vs Disconnected)
- Time-series de state

Formula: `uptime / total_time`.

### Latency
Response time percentiles:
- p50, p95, p99

### Error rate
- 5xx responses / total responses
- Timeouts as errors

### Throughput
- Requests per second
- Data transferred (MB/s)

## SLA (Service Level Agreement)
External commitment:
- Legal document con customers/business
- Penalties si violated

Orgs internal usually SLOs, not formal SLA.

## Measure SLIs

### Health checks
Scheduled synthetic transactions:
- Every 60 sec
- Call a low-cost backend endpoint via SCC
- Verify 200 response
- Log timing

### Passive monitoring
SCC access log parse:
- Count status codes
- Calculate percentiles
- Aggregate hourly

### Distributed tracing
End-to-end request tracking:
- Client → BTP app → SCC → backend → back
- Verify each hop within SLO

## Dashboards

### Grafana panels
- Availability gauge (green/red)
- Latency histogram
- Error rate line chart
- Throughput area chart

### Alerts
- Availability < 99% en last hour
- Latency p99 > 1 sec sustained
- Error rate > 5% for 5 min

## Error budget
Acceptable failure rate before violation.

99.9% SLO → 43 min/month error budget.

### Burning error budget rapidly?
→ Pause deployments, focus on stability.

### Budget healthy?
→ Accept more risk, ship faster.

## Compliance tracking
Monthly report to management:
- Availability actual vs target
- Incidents count
- Root causes
- Action items

## Postmortems
After major incidents:
- Timeline
- Root cause
- Mitigations
- Action items to prevent recurrence

Share across team, org.

## Capacity planning
Monitor:
- Request rate trend (growth)
- Peak load
- Time to saturation

Plan scale-up before hitting limits.

## Cost
SCC infrastructure cost tracked:
- Server hardware/VM
- Bandwidth
- Backup storage
- SAP support subscription

Correlate with usage (cost per request).

## Business context
SCC is enabler:
- Business apps depend on it
- Downtime = business impact

Quantify:
- $/hour of SCC downtime
- Users affected
- Revenue at risk

Justifies investment en HA, redundancy.

## Best practices
- **Realistic SLOs** — not 100%
- **Automate measurement** — no manual
- **Report regularly** — monthly / quarterly
- **Learn from misses** — postmortem, improve
- **Communicate proactively** — planned maintenance windows

title: SAP BTP: SAP Alerting service — event-based alerts
excerpt: Configurar alertas de BTP a external systems.
body:
## Overview
Alert Notification en BTP subscribes eventos de:
- CF apps (crashes, restarts)
- HANA Cloud (backups, alerts)
- Kyma (pod issues)
- Cloud Connector
- Custom apps

## Subscribe
BTP cockpit → subscribe **Alert Notification**.

## Create instance
```bash
cf create-service alert-notification standard my-alerts
```

## Configure destinations
BTP → **Alert Notification instance → Configuration**:

### Slack
- Webhook URL (Slack incoming webhook)
- Test message

### Microsoft Teams
- Connector webhook URL

### Email
- Recipient list
- Subject template

### Webhook (generic)
- Any HTTPS endpoint
- Auth options (Basic, Bearer)

### PagerDuty
- Integration key
- Escalation policy

## Subscriptions
Connect actions to filters:
- **Filter**: eventType.contains('crash') AND severity == 'FATAL'
- **Actions**: send to Slack + PagerDuty

## Custom events from app
```javascript
const axios = require('axios');

await axios.post(alertServiceUrl, {
    subject: 'Payment processing failed',
    body: 'Order 12345 payment failed after 3 retries',
    eventType: 'payment.error',
    severity: 'ERROR',
    priority: 'HIGH',
    resource: {
        resourceName: 'orders-service',
        resourceType: 'app',
        tags: { env: 'prod', team: 'payments' }
    }
}, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }
});
```

## Severity levels
- **FATAL** — critical, needs immediate attention
- **ERROR** — significant issue
- **WARNING** — potential problem
- **INFO** — informational

## Common patterns

### Health check failure
App health endpoint fails → alert.

### High error rate
Metrics threshold exceeded → alert.

### Cert expiring
30 days before → warn.
7 days → error.
1 day → fatal.

### Job failed
Batch job en Job Scheduler fails → alert.

### Business anomaly
Daily orders drop >50% → alert business team.

## Delivery guarantees
Best-effort. For critical alerts:
- Use multiple destinations (email + Slack + PagerDuty)
- Retry logic on client side

## Silencing
Avoid alert fatigue:
- Group similar alerts (same resource within 5 min)
- De-dup
- Silence during known maintenance

## Alert triage
### Runbook per alert type
- Diagnostic steps
- Common causes
- Escalation path

Alert message contains runbook link.

## Metrics
### Meta-alerts
- Alerts sent per day
- Response time to acknowledge
- False positive rate

## Best practices
- **Signal-to-noise ratio** — quality > quantity
- **Actionable alerts** — recipient can do something
- **Priority-based routing** — critical → PagerDuty, info → email
- **Alert on symptoms, not causes** — customer-facing issues
- **Regular review** — remove obsolete alerts

title: SAP BTP: managing global account con directories
excerpt: Estructurar global account con directories para governance.
body:
## Directories
Optional middle layer entre global account y subaccounts.

## Uses
- **Departmental separation** (Finance, HR, Sales)
- **Environment tiers** (Dev, QA, Prod)
- **Geographic** (AMER, EMEA, APJ)
- **Business unit**
- **Cost center alignment**

## Setup

### Enable directory features
Global account → **Directories → New Directory**:
- Name
- Description
- **Features** enable:
    - Entitlement management
    - Custom domain
    - Delegated authorization

### Nested directories
Directories can contain subdirectories.

Max practical: 3-4 levels deep.

## Entitlement management
Without directory: entitlements en global account, allocated a subaccounts directly.

Con directory feature enabled:
- Global → directories (sub-allocations)
- Directory → subaccounts

### Benefit
Delegation of quota management:
- Finance director controls Finance directory quota
- IT central just allocates budget to directory

## Delegated authorization
Directory admins manage their subaccounts without global access.

### Governance benefit
- Local decision-making
- Central oversight
- Segregation of duties

## Custom domain
Each directory can have own custom domain:
- `finance.empresa.com` for Finance directory apps
- `sales.empresa.com` for Sales

## Cost tracking
Costs aggregate by directory:
- Finance directory: $X/month
- Sales directory: $Y/month

Chargeback more granular.

## Common patterns

### 2-level (envs)
```
Global Account: ACME Corp
├── Directory: Development
│   ├── Subaccount: myapp-dev-01
│   ├── Subaccount: myapp-dev-02
├── Directory: Production
│   ├── Subaccount: myapp-prod-01
```

### 2-level (business units)
```
Global Account: ACME Corp
├── Directory: Finance
│   ├── Subaccount: fi-dev
│   ├── Subaccount: fi-prod
├── Directory: Sales
│   ├── Subaccount: sd-dev
│   ├── Subaccount: sd-prod
```

### 3-level (BU × Env)
```
Global Account: ACME Corp
├── Directory: Finance
│   ├── Directory: Finance-Dev
│   │   └── Subaccount: fi-dev
│   ├── Directory: Finance-Prod
│   │   └── Subaccount: fi-prod
├── Directory: Sales
```

More management but clearest separation.

## Admin roles

### Global Account admin
- Full access, everything
- Creates directories
- Assigns entitlements

### Directory admin
- Manages subaccounts within directory
- Delegates to subaccount admins

### Subaccount admin
- Manages users + services within subaccount

## Move subaccount between directories
BTP cockpit → subaccount → **Move**.

May have implications (entitlements, users). Test in non-prod.

## Migration to directories
Existing subaccounts sin directories → move to directory structure:
1. Plan structure
2. Create directories
3. Move subaccounts one by one
4. Verify no disruption

## Common issues

### 'Cannot create subaccount'
Quota exhausted at directory level. Check entitlements.

### 'Can't move subaccount'
Active resources may block. Coordinate with users.

### 'User cannot access directory'
Role collection assignment issue. Verify.

## Best practices
- **Plan structure first** — hard to change later
- **Consistent naming** — clear purpose
- **Documented ownership** — who owns each directory
- **Regular review** — structure fits current needs
- **Cost visibility** — align with budget structure

title: SAP BTP: multi-cloud deployment (AWS + Azure)
tags: btp, multi cloud, aws, azure, gcp
excerpt: Deploy BTP subaccounts en múltiples clouds.
body:
## BTP cloud providers
- **AWS** — original + widespread
- **Azure** — SAP partnership
- **GCP** — limited services
- **Alibaba Cloud** — China

## Region availability
Check service matrix — some services solo en certain providers.

### AWS regions comunes
- eu10 (Frankfurt)
- us10 (Ashburn)
- ap10 (Tokyo)
- ap11 (Singapore)
- br10 (São Paulo)

### Azure regions
- eu20 (Netherlands)
- eu21 (France)
- us20 (US East VA)
- us21 (US West)
- ap20 (Sydney)
- jp20 (Japan)

### GCP regions
- us30 (Iowa)

## Multi-cloud rationale
- **Data residency** — some countries require specific cloud
- **Cost arbitrage** — compare pricing
- **Redundancy** — cross-cloud DR
- **Compliance** — regulatory
- **Existing corporate cloud** — use same as rest of IT

## Deploy strategy
### Single subaccount, single cloud
Most common. Simple.

### Multiple subaccounts, different clouds
One per region/cloud combination:
- Subaccount A: eu10 (AWS)
- Subaccount B: eu20 (Azure)

## Data replication
HANA Cloud multi-region:
- Primary en one cloud
- Replica en another
- Automatic failover

## App deployment
Same code should deploy to any provider.

### CF portability
CF apps work en any BTP region regardless of provider.

### Provider-specific
Some services differ:
- Storage APIs (S3 vs Blob)
- Region-specific features

Abstract via SDKs when possible.

## Cross-cloud connectivity
### BTP does the heavy lifting
- Apps in AWS BTP calling Azure BTP: uses BTP internal network
- No public internet

### Cross-cloud via public
- Cost: egress fees
- Latency: higher

## Compliance
Check:
- GDPR (EU)
- LGPD (Brazil)
- Data sovereignty laws

Cloud provider certifications:
- AWS SOC 2, ISO 27001, etc.
- Azure similar
- Verify BTP-specific certifications

## Cost
Providers similar pricing. Small differences.

BTP margin on top.

Calculate para your workload.

## Common misconceptions

### 'BTP is cloud-agnostic'
Mostly true, but service availability varies. Verify.

### 'Multi-cloud = automatic DR'
No. Requires deliberate architecture (replication, failover).

## Cross-provider concerns
- **Networking** — inter-region latency (ocean crossings)
- **Data transfer** — costs adds up
- **Support** — different teams handle different clouds

## Best practices
- **Start simple** — one cloud, one region
- **Scale out** deliberately
- **Measure benefit** vs complexity
- **Documentation** — clear rationale para multi-cloud
- **Skills** — team needs expertise in each

## Vendor lock-in mitigation
Even within BTP, keep code portable:
- Standard OData
- Standard OAuth
- Avoid provider-specific features unless necessary

Enables migration if BTP-cloud-provider strategy changes.
